hook_1.message: Take a look at these two bars. Something is similar and something is different.

hook_2.message: What do you notice about the colored parts?

hook_redirect.message: Look at where the color ends on each bar — the top one and the bottom one. Do they stop at the same spot?

hook_retry.message: Now look again — do the colored parts take up the same amount of space?

hook_give.message: That's okay! The colored parts actually do end at the same spot. Even though one bar has more pieces, the colored amount is the same.

hook_confirm.message: Exactly! Different number of pieces, but the colored part is the same size.

define_1.message: When two fractions look different but mean the same amount, they're called equivalent fractions.

define_2.message: 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent. Different numbers, same amount colored. Let's learn how to find them!

shade_wait.message: Here's one whole bar. Tap it to color it in!
shade_wait.hint: Just tap once on the bar!

shade_confirm.message: Nice! That's one whole — 1 out of 1 piece colored.

cut_intro.message: Now watch — I'm cutting it into 2 equal pieces.

cut_reveal.message: Same amount is colored, but now there are 2 pieces. 1 out of 2 is colored — that's 1/2. Make sense?

cut_explain.message: Count the pieces — there are 2. Count the colored ones — there's 1. The colored piece is 1 out of 2.

cut_retry.message: So if 1 out of 2 pieces is colored, we write that as 1/2. Ready to keep going?

cut_explain_2.message: The bottom number is how many pieces total (2). The top number is how many are colored (1). So it's 1/2!

cut_confirm.message: When you cut a bar into more pieces, you can find a new fraction that means the same thing. Let's try it!

split_wait.message: I added a second bar below. Tap a piece in it two times quickly to cut it in half.
split_wait.hint: Tap the same piece two times quickly!

split_confirm.message: You cut it! One piece became two. Keep cutting until you have 4 pieces, then tap 2 of them to color them.

equiv_wait_1.message: Make the blue bar show 2/4 — four pieces, two colored.
equiv_wait_1.hint: Double-tap pieces to cut them. Single-tap to color them.

equiv_reveal_1.message: Look — the colored parts on both bars end at the same spot!

equiv_redirect_1.message: Look at the bars again. The colored parts on top and bottom — do they end at the same spot or different spots?

equiv_retry_1.message: If the colored parts end at the same spot, does that mean they're the same amount?

equiv_give_1.message: They are the same! The colored parts end at the same spot, which means 1/2 and 2/4 are the same amount — just cut into different sized pieces.

equiv_confirm_1.message: Yes! You found an equivalent fraction by cutting into more pieces. The colored amount stayed the same.

challenge_2_wait.message: Let's try a harder one. The top bar shows 2/3 — cut and color the purple bar until the colored parts match.
challenge_2_wait.hint: Try cutting into 6 pieces and coloring 4. See if the colored parts line up!

challenge_2_reveal.message: The colored parts line up again!

pattern_question.message: We keep cutting bars into more pieces but the colored amount stays the same. Why?

pattern_redirect.message: Look at the pieces in the bottom bar. They're smaller than the pieces in the top bar, right? But there are more of them colored.

pattern_retry.message: Smaller pieces, but more of them colored — does the total colored amount change?

pattern_give.message: It actually stays the same! Cutting makes smaller pieces, but you color more of them — so the total colored part doesn't change.

pattern_confirm.message: That's the secret! Cutting makes smaller pieces — but you color more of them. It balances out.

non_example_setup.message: But not all fractions are equivalent. Look at these two bars.

non_example_question.message: Do the colored parts end at the same spot?

non_example_redirect.message: Look again at the right edge of each colored part. The teal bar's color goes further than the coral bar's.

non_example_retry.message: So which colored part is bigger — the top bar or the bottom bar?

non_example_give.message: 3 is a bigger number than 2, but more pieces means each piece is smaller! The top bar's colored part is actually bigger. 1/2 is more than 1/3.

non_example_correct.message: Right! The colored parts don't line up — so 1/2 and 1/3 are not equivalent.

non_example_why.message: These bars have different numbers of pieces and different amounts colored. That's why they don't match.

assessment_intro.message: Time to test your skills! Three quick questions.

quiz_1_redirect.message: Let's look at the bars. See where the colored parts end on each one.

quiz_1_retry.message: 1/4 doesn't line up with 1/2. What about 3/6 — would 3 out of 6 pieces line up with 1 out of 2?

quiz_1_give.message: Look — 3 out of 6 takes up exactly the same space as 1 out of 2. They're equivalent!

quiz_1_right.message: 3 out of 6 — the colored parts line up with 1 out of 2!

quiz_2_redirect.message: Let's see. Here's 2/3 on top and 2/6 on the bottom. Look at the colored parts.

quiz_2_retry.message: 2/6 doesn't line up with 2/3 — the colored parts are different sizes. What about 4/6?

quiz_2_give.message: 4 out of 6 takes up the same space as 2 out of 3. They're equivalent!

quiz_2_right.message: 4 out of 6 matches 2 out of 3 — each top piece equals two bottom pieces!

quiz_3_redirect.message: Look at the bars. Count how many pieces are colored on each one.

quiz_3_retry.message: The top bar has 2 colored, the bottom has 3. Do the colored parts end at the same spot?

quiz_3_give.message: 2 colored vs 3 colored — the bottom bar has more color! They don't line up, so they're not equivalent.

quiz_3_right.message: 2 colored vs 3 colored — the bars don't line up, so they're not equivalent!

complete.message: You did it! Remember — if the colored parts line up, the fractions are equivalent. Great job today!
